Model Fitting on Imputed Data Sets

Source: R/miHelper-mi-fit-amelia.R, R/miHelper-mi-fit-data-frame.R, R/miHelper-mi-fit-list.R, and 3 more
MIFit.Rd

Model Fitting on Imputed Data Sets

Usage

# S3 method for class 'amelia'
MIFit(x, fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
MIFit(x, fit, M = 5, fun = "mice", ...)

# S3 method for class 'list'
MIFit(x, fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mids'
MIFit(x, fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'norm'
MIFit(x, fit, ...)

MIFit(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Object.

fit

Object. Output of the model fitting functions (e.g., lm(), lavaan::lavaan(), lavaan::cfa(), lavaan::sem()).

...

Additional arguments for MIFit.data.frame() to pass to fun. For "mcmcNorm": iter, the number of data augmentation cycles per imputation (default 1000); prior, "noninformative" (default) or "ridge"; and ridge_df, the degrees of freedom of the ridge prior (default 1).

M

Positive integer. Number of imputations for MIFit.data.frame().

fun

Character string. Select function to use for multiple imputation for MIFit.data.frame(). Valid values include "mice" for mice::mice(), "amelia" for Amelia::amelia(), and "mcmcNorm" for the multivariate normal model: EM, then data augmentation (Schafer, 1997), in C++ in this package.

Value

Returns an object of class mifit which is a list with the following elements:

mi

Multiply imputed data sets.

fit

List of models fitted on each imputed data set.

References

Li, K. H., Raghunathan, T. E., & Rubin, D. B. (1991). Large-sample significance levels from multiply imputed data using moment-based statistics and an F reference distribution. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 86 (416), 1065–1073. doi:10.1080/01621459.1991.10475152

Schafer, J. L. (1997). Analysis of incomplete multivariate data. Chapman & Hall/CRC. doi:10.1201/9780367803025

Rubin, D. B. (1987). Multiple imputation for nonresponse in surveys. John Wiley & Sons, Inc. doi:10.1002/9780470316696

See also

Other Multiple Imputation Helper Functions: MI2List(), MICombine()

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

fit <- lm(Temp ~ ., data = airquality)

# mice --------------------------------------
set.seed(42)
MIFit(
  x = airquality,
  fit = fit,
  fun = "mice",
  M = 3
)
